content: A Denturist, also known as a Dental Prosthetist or a Registered Clinical Dental Technician in some countries, is a specialized dental professional who constructs removable oral prostheses, such as dentures, directly for patients. Unlike dental technicians, Denturists do not typically work under the supervision or instruction of a dentist. Their scope of practice is generally limited to removable prostheses, and they may need to refer patients to a dentist for other types of dental care. It is important to note that Denturists are distinct from Prosthodontists, who are fully qualified specialist dentists trained to create both fixed and removable dental appliances. Denturists are trained to perform a variety of specific functions. These include conducting comprehensive oral examinations and evaluations, which involve obtaining a detailed medical and dental history of the patient. They are responsible for making impressions of the patient’s oral structures, recording necessary jaw relations, selecting artificial teeth, and designing the dentures. Additionally, Denturists provide adjunctive services such as repairing, relining, or adjusting removable dentures. They may also supervise auxiliary personnel in the performance of delegated tasks. To become a licensed Denturist, an individual must complete an accredited educational program, which typically lasts two to three years. In most jurisdictions, candidates are also required to have at least four years of prior experience in dental technology. The practice of Denturism involves the creation and fitting of artificial dentures and other removable dental appliances directly for patients. Denturism is a recognized profession in many parts of the world, allowing Denturists to provide affordable and professional denture care without the supervision of a dentist. The International Federation of Denturists represents national organizations worldwide that aim to advance the profession and improve access to denture care for the edentulous population. In the United States, Denturism is legislated and practiced in six states, including Maine, Arizona, Washington, Oregon, Montana, and Colorado, but it remains illegal in other states, such as Florida. In Canada, Denturism has been a regulated profession since 1973, with eight out of ten provinces recognizing it. The United Kingdom has also legislated the profession, where Denturists are referred to as Clinical Dental Technicians. These professionals are trained to design, create, and modify removable appliances, ensuring optimal fit, comfort, and overall well-being for patients. In Australia, the profession is similarly regulated, and Denturists are known as Dental Prosthetists. While Denturists often begin their careers as dental technicians, they undergo additional specialized training in Denturism. This advanced education equips them with the skills and knowledge necessary to work directly with patients, focusing exclusively on cases of edentulism and the associated oral anatomy. This background gives Denturists a unique advantage in their field. Denturists differ significantly from other dental professionals. University-trained dentists provide a full range of dental health care services, including assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of oral conditions. In contrast, Denturists focus solely on the clinical work related to prosthetic devices, such as dentures, and do not perform procedures involving natural teeth or oral tissues. Dental technicians, on the other hand, work in laboratories and are trained to fabricate dental appliances for dentists. Unlike Denturists, dental technicians do not have the technical training or legal authority to work directly with patients.
